note.name: Avalanche
note.thesis: AVAX has real institutional headlines, but its near-term usage economics are weak. Real users are scarce, activity is bot-heavy, and network fees are negligible against FDV while Q3 net issuance was about 2.56M AVAX. Supply and unlock pressure persist.
note.what: Avalanche is a proof-of-stake network. Its C-Chain runs EVM contracts, P-Chain coordinates validators, and X-Chain handles asset transfers. AVAX pays gas, secures the network via staking, and is the unit of account across Avalanche L1s; fees are burned. Institutions use it for tokenized assets.

points.text: NYSE selected Avalanche as core ledger for the clearing firm supporting its NYSE-affiliated tokenized-securities ATS.
Bitquery via AInvest: 95% of Q2 daily active addresses came from one wallet farm; bots sent 90-94% of activity by August; regulars fell to 21,506.
FDV is $4.01B. TTM network fees are about $2.85M; Q3 annualised network fees roughly $2.1M. App/protocol one-year fees are $120.54M but may not accrue to AVAX.
Q3 staking rewards were about 2.62M AVAX; burned fees were 59,126 AVAX, leaving net issuance of about 2.56M AVAX.
Helicon activation doubled median burn to 1,791 AVAX/day from 959; NYSE and Schwab give distribution; supply is capped at 720M.

note.supplyHeadline: Small scheduled unlocks, but issuance persists
note.supplyText: CoinGecko 11 Nov 2026: circulating 445.8M, total 470.9M, max 720M. DefiLlama 11 Nov 2026: 445.3M unlocked of 471.9M scheduled; next 90 days +1.7M Foundation; first new tokens 2027-01-25; cliff 2027-01-24 1.7M. Staked AVAX was about 198M, 42% of total supply, across 594 validators at Q3 end.
note.valuationText: FDV is $4.01B. TTM network fees are about $2.85M; Q3 annualised network fees roughly $2.1M. App/protocol one-year fees are $120.54M, but they may not accrue to AVAX. AVAX gas fees are burned, so network fees matter for supply. Peer median unavailable.
note.usageText: Q3 apps generated $27.2M fees and $7.25M revenue, first quarterly rise since Q3 2025; September fees were $10.4M. After Helicon, volume halved as bots left; humans did 74,629 tx/day at median fee $0.0041. Regulars fell to 21,506 in August.

catalysts.text: Helicon reward-curve change phases in, lowering minimum consumption from 10% to 7.5%.
Next scheduled Foundation unlock; 1.7M AVAX, 0.4% of CoinGecko circulating supply.

risks.title: NYSE ATS launches
risks.text: A dated NYSE tokenized ATS launch with measurable AVAX fee capture would undercut the bear case.

risks.title: Burn keeps rising
risks.text: Median daily burn holds above 1,791 AVAX and network fees accelerate after Helicon.

risks.title: Institutional demand absorbs supply
risks.text: Schwab distribution and tokenized-asset demand offset Foundation unlocks and net issuance.

risks.title: Real users return
risks.text: Regular addresses recover from 21,506 and bot share falls, improving fee quality.

watchlist.item: Foundation 1.67M AVAX unlock already landed 8 Nov 2026

note.positioningText: Funding is -0.0422%/8h now and -0.0015%/8h on a 7-day average, so shorts pay longs. Open interest is $76M, up 9.0% over 7 days. The long/short account ratio is 2.25, with 69% of accounts long. Positioning is mixed.
note.conclusion: The NYSE and Schwab headlines are real, but AVAX's near-term economics are weak. Real users are scarce, activity is bot-heavy, and network fees are negligible against FDV. Q3 net issuance was about 2.56M AVAX, and the next scheduled Foundation unlock adds supply. Helicon's burn improvement and institutional distribution are the main risks to the bear view.
note.invalidation: 7-day annualised network fees hold above Q3 annualised $2.1M for two weeks.
note.gaps: Peer FDV and fee/revenue data were not available, so the valuation comparison is incomplete. Direct team, foundation or investor sale data was not found. NYSE ATS launch date, governance votes, Robinhood Chain Q3 DEX volume and Ondo Anthropic were not found.
